    "rationale": "Evidence: all 180 development trials across iterations 0 to 2 ended off_track with no finishes. Iteration 1 (5 sensors at 8 mm spacing, y=0.03, kp 2.0, kd 0.2, base 1.5) was best at 65.9. Max error sits at about 0.061 to 0.064 on every track, just past the 0.06 m limit, and line_loss_events are 1 to 2 per run. The line loss is the likely trigger: with 8 mm footprints at x=±0.016, a sensor sees tape only while its centre is within about 0.0165 m of the line, so an offset of about 1.7 cm blinds every sensor. The robot then coasts at reduced throttle (0.35) on a weak search, and the error grows past 0.06. Iteration 2 widened the spread to ±0.024 with 8 mm footprints, but it also raised kp to 2.5, moved sensors to y=0.05 and lowered kd to 0.1, and it scored worse (49.9). That suggests the added gain and the forward offset hurt more than the wider spread helped, so I should not simply repeat it.\n\nChanges from iteration 1: (1) Sensor footprint 8 mm to 16 mm, and spread from ±0.016 to ±0.036 m at 12 mm pitch (seven sensors). A 16 mm footprint at x=±0.036 reaches tape while the robot is offset about 0.06 m, which keeps the line visible through the failure window. (2) Sensor y kept at 0.03, the position that scored best. (3) Weights [-2,-1.3,-0.6,0,0.6,1.3,2] keep the signal bounded and proportional to lateral error. (4) Because the wider pitch lowers the signal slope to about 55 per metre (iteration 1 was about 125 per metre), kp rises from 2.0 to 4.0 to keep the steering authority similar. (5) kd kept at 0.2, which was the best damping setting; ki kept at 0.05. (6) base_speed reduced from 1.5 to 1.4: survival is the bottleneck, and speed can be raised once the robot stays on track. Mass 0.7, body 0.12 by 0.18, wheel track 0.12, and radius 0.03 are unchanged, as is line_loss 'last_direction'.\n\nExpected result: line_loss_events fall to 0 or 1 per run, max_error drops below 0.06 on oval and s-bend, and progress rises above 0.3. Hypotheses: H1, line loss, not steering error, causes the off-track exits, so wider and larger sensors should cut them. H2, the 16 mm footprint blurs the centroid for small offsets, which may raise rms_error slightly. H3, kp 4.0 at this slope gives a steering response similar to iteration 1. Measurements to check: line_loss_events per track, max_error on s-bend and slalom, steering_oscillation (watch for kp too high), and progress. If the robot now survives but is slow, raise base_speed; if it oscillates, lower kp toward 3.0 before touching kd.",
